    "file": "shopapi/basket.py",
    "line": 20,
    "category": "Integrity / Deserialisation",
    "title": "Client-controlled pickle deserialisation enables arbitrary code execution",
    "description": "The basket cookie is supplied by the client and is passed to pickle.loads after only Base64 decoding. A crafted pickle payload can execute attacker-controlled globals in the application process whenever a basket endpoint reads the cookie.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/basket.py:15-23 calls pickle.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(raw)) without a signature or integrity check; with_basket at lines 26-28 writes the same untrusted format. This is an inherent remote-code-execution path through the basket cookie."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 101,
    "category": "Authentication",
    "title": "Token refresh accepts unsigned attacker-controlled JWT claims",
    "description": "The refresh endpoint disables JWT signature verification, trusts the supplied sub claim, and issues a newly signed token for that user. An attacker can name another existing user and obtain an authenticated token for that account.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/auth.py:100-107 calls jwt.decode(token, options={\"verify_signature\": False}), loads the user from claims.get(\"sub\"), and calls make_token(user). An unsigned JWT with sub=1 was accepted by POST /auth/refresh and returned a signed token."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 55,
    "category": "Authentication / Error handling",
    "title": "Authentication failures are swallowed and protected handlers continue",
    "description": "require_auth catches every Exception, including the 401 HTTPException raised when no valid user is present, then invokes the protected handler with g.user set to None. Any protected handler that does not immediately dereference g.user is therefore publicly reachable.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/auth.py:51-58 catches around abort(401), sets g.user=None, and still returns f(*args, **kwargs). GET /giftcards/HFDEMO10 without Authorization returned HTTP 200 with the gift-card balance despite the route's @require_auth decorator."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/orders.py",
    "line": 49,
    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Authenticated users can view other customers' orders",
    "description": "The individual order endpoint authenticates the caller but retrieves the requested order with get_order rather than own_order. Any authenticated customer who guesses an order ID can access another customer's order status, contents, payment amount, and refunds.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/orders.py:46-50 returns order_json(get_order(order_id)); the ownership check exists separately in own_order at lines 32-35 but is not used. A GET /orders/1 using a token for a different customer returned HTTP 200 and disclosed order details."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/__init__.py",
    "line": 37,
    "category": "Access control",
    "title": "Trailing slash bypasses the admin authorization check",
    "description": "The global staff check compares request.path to registered route strings. The refunds route accepts both slash forms, but /admin/refunds/ is not equal to the registered /admin/refunds string, so the staff check is skipped and the administrative refund handler runs anonymously.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/__init__.py:26 and :36-41 authorize only on exact path membership. shopapi/admin.py:52 defines /admin/refunds with strict_slashes=False. An unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ with an order_id and amount returned 200 and created a refund."
  },

    "category": "Injection",
    "title": "Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection",
    "description": "The search value is concatenated into a SQL statement rather than bound as a parameter. An attacker can alter the WHERE clause and retrieve unintended product rows or exploit SQLite query behavior.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/products.py:40-42 builds SQL using string concatenation. GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned all six products, demonstrating altered query semantics."
  },
  {

    "category": "Injection",
    "title": "Stored review content is rendered as trusted HTML",
    "description": "Authenticated users can store arbitrary review bodies, which are rendered with the Jinja safe filter without sanitisation. A malicious reviewer can persist JavaScript or markup that executes for visitors to the product page.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/products.py:82-91 stores body directly, and shopapi/templates/product.html:13 renders r.body with |safe. Posting a review containing <script>alert(1)</script> succeeded and the product page returned the script tag unescaped."
  },

    "title": "Customer display names enable SQL injection in the admin review report",
    "description": "The report interpolates a customer's mutable display name into a SQL WHERE clause. A customer can set a display name containing SQL syntax, then induce SQL execution when staff view that customer's report.",
    "evidence": "shopapi/admin.py:74-80 loads display_name and inserts it into an f-string SQL query. shopapi/auth.py:116-125 lets authenticated users set arbitrary display names up to 60 characters without escaping; the report is reached at /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=... ."
  },

    "title": "Approved image URLs can redirect the server to internal addresses",
